pairs.subject: on-stream-overlay-delivery
pairs.evidence: packages/stage-kit/src/ui/VotePanel.tsx:19 The on-stream vote panel works out its own bars from a Poll object that carries per-viewer ballots seen in chat. It does not just draw a share/count snapshot computed by the tool, which is the 'page computes its own aggregate from raw records' failure that aggregate-only-payloads names.

techniques.evidence: packages/stage-kit/src/ui/VotePanel.tsx:19 Bars (weight, %, rank bands) are computed in the page from the poll, including chat-observed ballots. The page is not handed closed aggregate fields.

packages/stage-kit/src/ui/ChatLane.tsx:55 The chat lane runs the runtime's ballot rule again for each viewer on the page so it can label vote chips. The page becomes a second state machine that has to track the tool's rule exactly, which is the failure the technique names.

pairs.registryProposal: The standard's aggregate-only rule forbids joining a visible name to how that person voted on stream. But a chat lane drawing a viewer's own public '!vote 2' line, with a 'VOTE 2 · <option>' chip (ChatLane.tsx:125/133), repeats something the viewer already said in public chat. The technique should say whether a public chat-command echo counts as the viewer's own consenting act, or whether it is still the forbidden join.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/pages/characters/routes.ts:3 These 'packages' are character definitions browsed in the operator console. They are not design packages an overlay renders.

pairs.subject: on-stream-overlay-delivery
pairs.evidence: packages/stage-kit/src/sceneModel.ts:145 The scene the broadcast page builds keeps a viewer-id → option book of individual ballots, built from raw chat events in the page. So the overlay's data holds who voted for what, which aggregate-only payloads keeps out of the overlay's data entirely.

techniques.evidence: packages/stage-kit/src/sceneModel.ts:145 The overlay page's state holds individual ballots keyed by viewer id. The feed is raw chat events with viewer ids, names and ranks.

packages/stage-kit/src/tallies.ts:63 Until an authoritative tally arrives, the page's own count from folded chat events sets the bar weight. That is a second counter that re-implements the runtime rule (scene.ts:195 builds voters from msg.viewer.id). It is not a full snapshot from the tool.
